_comment: Machines run_linters.py --remote may use (surveyed read-only 2026-11-02). Capabilities are PROBED at run time (lint_remote.probe); the fields here say how to reach a machine, how hard it may be pushed and why a machine is not a lint runner. Nothing here is a secret: keys are named by path and never read.

devbox.note: This development machine. Always capable (it has the full toolchain); all other machines are optional.

mac1-vm.note: Debian 13 arm64 Lima VM hams-test-debian on the Mac mini mac1 (Bruce's machine; the VM also runs the production FCC ULS sync): lowest priority, 3 workers, never started by the lint runner (a stopped VM is reported unreachable). Has cargo, node, chromium, flake8, odoo, rsync; pytest is installed per user by tools/lint_remote_provision.sh.

bruce-yoga.note: Debian 13 x86-64 build and test server (8 cores, GitHub Actions runner bruce-yoga-linux). Stays awake on AC (logind drop-in); on battery it may suspend, which shows as unreachable. Has python3 and chrome only: run tools/lint_remote_provision.sh for flake8, pytest, node, cargo.

mac1.reason: macOS host and Bruce's own machine; its Linux VM mac1-vm is the lint runner. System python is 3.9 (the linters need 3.10+), no cargo or node.

bruce-yoga-win.reason: Windows build VM behind bruce-yoga (PowerShell, no POSIX tar/sh pipeline); used for Windows relay builds only.

Bruce_Thinkpad.reason: Windows laptop (PowerShell); used for Windows relay builds and the Windows side of certificate login.

hams1.reason: PRODUCTION. Never a lint, test or build host.
